title: Map the buying committee
notice: Demo with sample data only. It is not connected to your organization's data, and it should not be.
question: Map the synthetic Acme buying committee and show the relationship gaps without creating outreach tasks.

answer.question: Map the synthetic Acme buying committee and show the relationship gaps without creating outreach tasks.
answer.answer:
Here's the Acme buying committee map — read-only, nothing sent or logged anywhere:

**8 stakeholders identified:**

| Name | Role | Influence | Score | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sarah Chen | CTO (New) | Decision Maker | 95 | **No intro yet** |
| James Miller | VP Operations | Champion | 85 | Champion |
| Lisa Park | CFO | Economic Buyer | 90 | Needs ROI |
| David Wong | IT Director | Influencer | 70 | Positive |
| Rachel Torres | Procurement | Gatekeeper | 50 | Neutral |
| Kevin Park | VP Engineering | Influencer | 60 | Positive |
| Maria Lopez | Director of Strategy | Influencer | 40 | **No contact** |
| Tom Bradley | CEO | Executive Sponsor | 80 | Aware only |

**Key relationship gaps:**
- **Sarah Chen (CTO)** — controls the tech budget, highest influence score (95), but no existing relationship. Biggest blind spot.
- **Lisa Park (CFO)** — economic buyer, still waiting on a solid business case/ROI.
- **Maria Lopez** — no contact at all, lower influence but unmapped.

You have one strong asset: James Miller (VP Ops) is already a champion and could bridge an intro to Sarah Chen.

No outreach tasks, emails, or CRM changes were created — this is just the map. Want me to pull competitive intel next, or go straight to value messaging/objection handling for these personas?
